questions.question: Where should the weekly client status update go?
options: Where the client reads it: the shared client channel or email
A 1:1 chat with the dev lead
The internal Dev channel
questions.explanation: Status goes to the client-facing place, not an internal channel or a private chat.

prompt: Order the steps for running a review meeting with an external client in Teams.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: Tell attendees, then start recording and transcript
Schedule it and invite the client's email address
Post a recap: decisions, actions, owners, dates
Send the agenda before the call
Set meeting options: lobby and who can present

task.explanation: Invite, lock down the options, set the agenda, record with consent, then follow up in writing.

prompt: You set up a sprint review with Acme (external client). Flag the meeting options you should change.

cells: People in my org and guests

rows.issue: With external attendees, limit presenting to organisers or named people.
Agree recording with the client up front rather than recording by default.

questions.question: Acme's CEO has no Teams account. What do you tell her?
options: She can usually join from the link in a browser
She must buy a Teams licence
She must be added to your organisation
questions.explanation: External people can normally join from the invite link in a browser or the free app, subject to your admin's settings.

prompt: Your sprint review was a channel meeting in Acme Portal › Sprints, recorded with transcript on. Answer the questions.

questions.question: Where is the recording of this channel meeting stored?
options: In the channel's Files (SharePoint)
Only on the organiser's laptop
In each attendee's inbox
Nowhere; it expires at once
questions.explanation: Channel meeting recordings are saved to the channel's SharePoint folder, shown in its Files tab.

questions.question: A transcript is available. What is it best used for?
options: Checking exact wording of decisions before writing minutes
Replacing minutes; nobody needs a summary
Client sign-off of scope
questions.explanation: A transcript is raw evidence; minutes still need a short summary of decisions and actions.

questions.question: The client missed the call. What do you send?
options: A short recap of decisions and actions, linking the recording if they have access
The full transcript with no summary
Nothing; it was recorded
questions.explanation: Lead with what was decided and who does what; the recording is backup.

prompt: Acme's product owner wants to talk to your devs directly in Teams. Your internal team's channels hold estimates, margins and notes on other clients.

steps.question: How do you set this up?
options: A client-facing shared channel or team, with Acme added there only
Add Acme as a guest to your internal team
Give Acme a company account
Refuse; email only
steps.explanation: Give the client a dedicated space so internal channels stay internal.

steps.question: The project ends next month. What about their access?
options: Remove it at close, after handing over the files they need
Leave it; guests cost nothing
Delete the channel without notice
Convert them to full members
steps.explanation: Access should end with the engagement, after a clean handover.

prompt: A PM describes how they run a client project in Teams. Mark the practices that will cause problems.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.text: One team per client project, with channels for Dev, QA and Releases.
Decisions are made and kept in 1:1 chats with the relevant dev.
segments.issue: Decisions in private chats are invisible to the team and lost later.

segments.text: The client is in a separate client-facing channel only.
Project files live in the channel's Files tab, not personal OneDrive.
Client meetings are recorded by default without mentioning it.
segments.issue: Tell attendees and agree before recording.

segments.text: Build notifications post to the Releases channel.
Former contractors keep guest access after they leave, just in case.
segments.issue: Remove access when people leave the project.

prompt: You're running a requirements call with a new client and want a recording and transcript to write the minutes from.

steps.question: Before starting the recording you:
options: Say it will be recorded and transcribed, why, and ask for objections
Start it quietly; Teams shows a banner anyway
Record on your phone instead
Record only the internal pre-call
steps.explanation: Ask openly; the banner is not consent.

steps.question: Midway the client says: "Off the record, our real budget is lower." You:
options: Pause recording and transcript, and keep it out of shared minutes
Keep recording; it helps the proposal
Put it in the minutes in bold
End the meeting
steps.explanation: Respect the request and keep it out of anything shared.

prompt: When should a project discussion be in a channel rather than a group chat?

options: When the whole project team needs to see it and find it later
When it's urgent
When it's private between two people
Never; chats are always better
mcq.explanation: Channels are organised by topic, visible to the team and searchable; chats suit quick, private or ad-hoc talk.

prompt: A guest in your organisation's Teams is:

options: Someone outside your organisation added to a team with limited access
Any colleague without a licence
A Teams admin
A bot
mcq.explanation: Guests are external people invited into a team; they see only that team, with fewer permissions.

prompt: What does turning on transcription in a Teams meeting give you?

options: A searchable text record of who said what, saved with the meeting
An approved set of minutes
A translation of all shared files
A recording of shared screens only
mcq.explanation: A transcript is a speaker-attributed record; minutes still need writing and checking.

prompt: Main benefit of a shared channel with a client over adding them as a guest?

options: They work from their own Teams organisation without switching accounts
They see all your other channels
No admin settings are needed
Recordings are turned off
mcq.explanation: Shared channels let people from another organisation join one channel from their own Teams, with no tenant switching.
